items.statement: Targets Rs 375-400 crore revenue for FY26, implying 25-33% growth over FY25
items.quote: we are looking at a target of about Rs. 375 crores to Rs. 400 crores this year

items.statement: Expects 40-50% revenue growth in FY27 over FY26
items.quote: in the upcoming year as I said we are looking at least 40% to 50% growth over this year, for the next year

items.statement: Aims to reach Rs 1,000 crore revenue within next 3-4 years
items.quote: we are looking at how we can achieve the Rs. 1000 crores revenue is the target that we have taken for ourselves. In next maximum three to four years, we should be there

items.statement: Unexecuted order book stands at Rs 695 crore as of today, including Rs 439 crore of recent orders
items.quote: as of today we have about Rs. 695 crores of unexecuted order book which also includes Rs. 439 crores of orders which we have recently received

items.statement: Plans to execute ~Rs 500 crore from current order book in FY27
items.quote: approximately we are planning to do about Rs. 500 crores of work will be done in the next financial year

items.statement: Maintains unexecuted order book at ~150% of prior year revenue; expects Rs 300-600 crore order book plus Rs 300-500 crore pipeline at any time
items.quote: by and large at any given point of time we would have a Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 600 crores of unexecuted order book and another Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 500 crores as in pipeline

items.statement: Margins steady due to cost-plus contracts with private clients; profitability grows only via volume
items.quote: our margins will remain always same. As I have been always saying we work very transparently, with the clients. Since we majorly operate with private players, wherein we work very transparently. practically on a cost plus basis because of that our margins are pretty steady

items.statement: Two tunnel projects nearing completion; one to finish this year, enabling direct NHAI bidding eligibility of Rs 500 crore single tender
items.quote: we are about to complete our two major tunnel projects one out of that will be completed this year which will also give us the credentials and credibility, wherein we could also bid on our own directly to the NHAI for the larger projects

items.statement: Additional INR35 crores (INR2 crores per store) for marketing/branding over 8-18 months per store
items.quote: Other than that INR287 crores capex we are set aside INR35 crores for 15 locations for exclusive branding of those locations

items.statement: EBITDA margin may dip 100-300 bps for ~30 months due to marketing spend; absolute EBITDA to rise
items.quote: there may be some dent of the 100 or 200 basis point , but otherwise in absolute value or absolute rupee term it will be higher than the current

items.statement: Gross profit margin on jewellery sales around 30-32%; industry operating margin 30-40%
items.quote: our gross profit margin on the jewellery sale will be around 30% to 32%

items.statement: Q3 revenue INR144.18 crores, EBITDA INR33.71 crores, PAT INR23.11 crores; 9M revenue INR300.90 crores
items.quote: Revenue from operation for only quarter 3 was INR144.18 crores with EBITDA of INR33.71 crores and PAT of INR23.11 crores

items.statement: Studded jewellery >95% of revenue; gold/platinum <5%; 95%+ from small diamonds (melee)
items.quote: total studded jewellery we are handling with. We are not selling gold jewellery and platinum jewellery we are selling but that is less than 5% of our total top line

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds impact solitaire/large stones; minimal threat to melee/small diamond designs (>95% of book)
items.quote: lab grown has impacted that studs or that solitaire kind of the stone rather than the small stones which are getting used for creating designs

items.statement: War/supply chain: no scarcity of gold/diamonds; minor price impact from USD/INR; demand impact uncertain
items.quote: there is no such kind of scarcity or anything in the market except little bit price upward movement may be there for the diamond due to the exchange rate

items.statement: Store breakeven: 12-18 months in Maharashtra, 18-24 months outside Maharashtra
items.quote: If it is within state it will take around 12 to 18 months for getting breakeven. If it is outside Maharashtra it will be somewhere 18 to 24 months

items.statement: Inventory ~70% of store capex; COCO store Q3 revenue INR2.5 crores (first quarter)
items.quote: Inventory consists almost 70% of our total capex

items.statement: Seasonality: H1 ~35% revenue, H2 ~65% due to festivals (Navratri, Diwali, Christmas, Valentine's)
items.quote: Generally H1 will have around 35% and 60% to 65% in H2 as it has got many festivals

items.statement: Board and management confirm no material governance or operational issues; resignation attributed to relationship issues, not substantive matters
items.quote: Based on our discussions, there was no specific happenings and practices that were brought to our attention. There were no specific operational or other issues that have been highlighted.

items.statement: RBI approved Keki Mistry as Interim Part-Time Chairman for 3 months to stabilize governance
items.quote: The Reserve Bank of India has approved my appointment as the Interim Part-Time Chairman for a period of 3 months.

items.statement: CEO reappointment process will proceed as normal; NRC to meet in near future
items.quote: As regards Sashi's appointment, it is something that will be considered by the remuneration committee, by the nomination and remuneration committee. There is still time to do that and obviously at the appropriate time, the committee will meet and we will take it up in the board.

items.statement: Management team unity affirmed; Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha to get more responsibilities
items.quote: There is complete, let me repeat, complete and absolute unity in the management team.

items.statement: Board committees (Audit, Risk, NRC) functioning effectively with independent oversight
items.quote: These are all manned by independent directors with strong vintage, credibility, experience, and stature. And some of them are on this call and they have, as I said, they have very comfortable with the functioning of these committees who in turn oversees the operations in every aspect of it.

items.statement: Anonymous complaints and social media allegations reviewed by Audit Committee and whistleblower mechanism; appropriate actions taken
items.quote: All of these complaints or references in social media which impact bank, the prominent ones, are examined and brought before the Audit Committee. Audit Committee deliberates on it and sends it to whistle-blower if it is that or some other kind of mechanism which exists in the bank.

items.statement: Economy in sweet spot; bank well positioned for growth trajectory recovery post-merger
items.quote: I continue to maintain and I am sure you have heard Keki in the past; the economy probably is in a sweet spot amidst turmoil in the world. The bank is now well positioned. We had a trajectory and we are on path to that trajectory.

items.statement: Technology investments to differentiate and surprise positively over next 1-2 years
items.quote: Technology is going to be differentiator, and you will see it more happening over the year and two. And that is going to be kind of a surprise to all of us, and to you as well.

items.statement: Board to meet soon to decide on new Chairman and Independent Director replacement in consultation with RBI and SEBI
items.quote: The Board will of course meet in due course, take the various regulators into confidence, and then take a call on the new chairman. There is still 3 months to go. For 3 months, I will remain the interim Chairman.

items.statement: Outgoing Chairman Atanu Chakraborty did not provide specific reasons for resignation despite repeated board inquiries
items.quote: We had repeatedly asked him for, you know, to tell us why what had triggered this and if there was anything we have to set it right, but he said there was nothing and that was a bit baffling.

items.statement: FY26 production target revised to 19-20 lakh tons from earlier 23.5 lakh tons due to project delays
items.quote: This year target we had revised to 23.5 lakhs not 25, okay. And we have come and we'll not be able to reach 23.5 lakhs this year. It will be lesser than that, it would be somewhere between 19 to 20, okay.

items.statement: FY27 production target set at 25 lakh tons for the whole company
items.quote: But definitely next year's target is 25 lakhs and we are working on that.

items.statement: Balaghat mine production target 4 lakh tons in FY27 after high-speed shaft commissioning
items.quote: Yeah, Balaghat, then in INR25 lakhs or INR4 lakhs is the production from Balaghat.

items.statement: Five shaft sinking projects awarded at total cost of INR664 crores to improve infrastructure and achieve production targets
items.quote: Total of around INR664 crores of investment is put into the shaft sinking projects so that our infrastructure can be improved and production targets can be achieved in the future.

items.statement: Central region demand of 2.8-3 million tons with room for MOIL to grow by another 1.5 million tons within the region
items.quote: So what I see is that even next three, four years' production, we will be we won't need to go to Vizag or Calcutta, that that zone. We are very comfortable in taking care of the Central region requirement.

items.statement: Stable operating margins maintained over last five years supported by strong demand and efficient operations
items.quote: As we can see that we have a stable operating margin during the last five years. And due to the strong performance and efficient operation and strong demand, which are supported in maintaining this stable margin.

items.statement: Prices kept 5-6% higher than imported prices; price increases applied across all grades including low-grade
items.quote: In fact, we keep the prices higher by about 5% to 6%. Because as I explained earlier, Raipur customers if they import, then they will have to incur higher logistic cost. So we take similar increase, rather we take 2% more.

items.statement: High-grade (above 30%) constitutes 45-50% of production, fines 15-20%, balance low-grade; low-grade sales growing 50% annually
items.quote: Generally, sir, the ore that is above 30% is considered as high grade and roughly 45% to 50% depending upon the area where we are mining, that will be high grade. And generally 15% to 20% will be the fines and the remaining is the low-grade ore in the total production.

items.statement: Balaghat high-speed shaft sinking completed, equipping done, winder installation ongoing; expected operational in 6 months (H1 FY27)
items.quote: Sinking is already completed, equipping is also completed, and the winders' installation is going on. So I expect by it will take another six months in the next financial year to make it operational.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 2,910 crores as of March 11, 2026, up from INR 283 crores in FY25, with net addition of over INR 1,200 crores since September 30, 2025
items.quote: as of March 11th, 2026 our order book stands at approximately INR2910 crores, reflecting a strong order inflow and a long -term customer commitment.

items.statement: Weatherford order of INR 1,030 crores has execution timeline of 3-5 years with staggered ramp-up starting at INR 80-100 crores in year 1 reaching INR 250-300 crores annually
items.quote: So basically it will start something from INR80 crores to INR100 crores and it will eventually go to a INR250 crores, INR300 crores.

items.statement: Management targets 35-40% revenue CAGR over next 2-3 years, consistent with historical growth, supported by capacity expansion and order book visibility
items.quote: historically we were in around 35% to 40% of a CAGR growth in the previous few years. So we are anticipating and we are trying our -- having the same growth line in the coming years.

items.statement: Capacity increased 40-50% in existing plant during FY26 (mostly Q3), with further capacity additions planned from IPO proceeds; new Sanand land (60,000 sqm) secured for expansion beyond FY28
items.quote: we have added in the present plant also we have increased our capacity is around 40% to 50% as compared to FY '25. FY '26 we have increased and some of the increase we have done in the quarter 3 of this year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 38.1% from 32.5% YoY; 9M FY26 EBITDA margin at 33.4% vs 31.7% YoY; management indicates sustainable range of 33-38%
items.quote: EBITDA margin increased to 38.1% from 32.5%.

items.statement: Raw material cost ~30% of revenue; marginal cost increases fully passed through to customers; no significant raw material risk
items.quote: overall in our cost structure, materials contributes less than 30% of the total cost average. So that is only the impact if there is anything.

items.statement: Energy segment (54% of revenue) driven by O&M (repeatable) not exploration; motion control & automation (27%) and industrial equipment (16%) growing; defense, gas turbine, renewables identified as growth vectors
items.quote: we are lot into maintenance, development and operations. So that is a continuity of the business what we have year-on-year. And in fact, if you see the numbers, we have been growing regularly in that particular domain as well.

items.statement: No product >7% of revenue; top 5 customers <25% each; diversified across energy, motion control, industrial equipment; build-to-print model with process engineering IP (5-micron accuracy) as differentiator
items.quote: our product segment is not highly depend on a particular product line. We have a very good diversified portfolio.

items.statement: Logistics lead time increased 7-12 days due to shipping constraints; ex-works terms limit direct impact; geopolitical uncertainty noted but order book provides visibility
items.quote: in terms of the logistic lead time, it has been improved -- increased around 7 to 12 days.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved to 256 days (6M FY26) from 283 days (FY25); inventory days decreasing as volumes ramp against MOQ constraints
items.quote: For 6 mont hs financial year '26 our net working capital cycle stood to 256 days compared to 283 days in the financial '25, reflecting a clear improvement in our working capital management.

items.statement: Targeting 15-20% growth in pump segment (ex-nuclear) for CY2026 based on current order book
items.quote: Yeah, we are aiming for that kind of growth in this year based on our order book position.

items.statement: Expecting minimum 2 to maximum 4 nuclear pumps to be invoiced in CY2026 if testing proceeds as planned
items.quote: So, I hope at least minimum two, maximum four pumps we should be able to invoice in this year if all goes as per plan.

items.statement: Solar business revenue was ₹189 crore in CY24, ₹245 crore in CY25, planning over ₹300 crore in CY26
items.quote: Yes, first CY '24 I think it was ₹189 crore. Last year it was ₹245 crores. This year we are planning much higher, more than ₹300 crores.

items.statement: CY27 solar growth contingent on KUSUM 2.0 approval; replacement category expected to drive volume
items.quote: CY '27 onwards, we presume that this KUSUM 2.0 Yojana, this will continue. There will be similar there have been announcement in the budget and as well as later on.

items.statement: Targeting to maintain EBITDA margin at 13-14% while focusing on top-line growth
items.quote: We want to maintain our healthy EBITDA level of around 13%, 14% which we are there. We are more focused of growth in the top line and keeping this EBITDA level at this level of 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Standard business (50%) can pass on cost increases; nuclear has PVC clause; domestic project business (30%) has low risk for CY26 as most equipment ordered
items.quote: Yeah, of course, it is very natural that for our standard business, which is 50% of the business, we can pass on this increase. But the remaining 50% is project business. So except the nuclear business where there is a PVC clause, there we are safeguarded.

items.statement: Supply chain risk from Middle East disruption: LPG/gas restrictions affecting foundry operations; exports to Middle East may be temporarily hampered
items.quote: I wouldn't say that we are not affected that that impacts has started coming a bit in the supply chain, especially in the foundries where there is restriction of the LPG and the gas supply, our furnaces are gas fired.

items.statement: First central warehouse started in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar; in-house solar controller manufacturing begun; S/4HANA implementation underway
items.quote: First central warehouse which we have started in Chhatrapati SambhajiNagar and supply chain diversification of the key components that is what we have achieved. And you can see the product range what we are offering into solar business, which includes solar controller as we discussed

items.statement: Order intake mix: 48% standard pumps, 19% engineered pumps, 15% SupremeServ, 18% valves; new products (solar, firefighting, water) driving majority of growth
items.quote: If you see the 2025 chart around 48% is standard pump, engineered pumps would be around 19%, SupremeServ around 15% and valves is around 18%. So overall bifurcation of order intake actually.

items.statement: Export margins better than domestic due to higher price levels and currency depreciation benefit; 70-80% export transactions via group companies
items.quote: Yes. I would say it has to be from a related party transaction. It has to be and but, yes, the price levels are much better outside than in India, I would say, definitely.

items.statement: Export target 25% of revenue (ex-nuclear) in good years; 30% possible but requires 2+ years to improve on-time delivery and quality
items.quote: Right now, we are trying 25%, I would say. But 30% in a good year is also possible. But it will take some time. It will take some time because as I said on time delivery and quality is still work in progress.

items.statement: Nuclear order book of ₹1,300 crore to be delivered over three years.
items.quote: But today, if you see, we have an order on hand of ₹1,300 crores, which we feel we will deliver it in the three years.

items.statement: Nuclear revenue could be ₹300-400 crore per year in a good year, varying from ₹100-150 crore.
items.quote: In a good year, it could be ₹300 crores, ₹400 crores maybe per year. So it will vary. It could vary from 100, 150 to 300 per year, 300 maybe more, depending on how the fast the business develops or comes up.

items.statement: Solar business expected to grow at least 20-25% with minimum ₹300 crore revenue this year.
items.quote: At least 20% minimum, 20% to 25%. Solar, it is normal, I would say. So, we are expecting at least minimum ₹300 crores this year.

items.statement: Aftermarket (SupremeServ) share is 15% of revenue, targeting 25-30%.
items.quote: No, no, that is SupremeServ revenue today almost is 15%.

items.statement: Aftermarket share target 25-30%.
items.quote: So if you ask me a figure, 25%, 30% is something which we want to grow because you see, we are going into mining.

items.statement: Export margins are better than domestic due to higher price levels and currency depreciation.
items.quote: Yes. I would say it has to be from a related party transaction. It has to be and but, yes, the price levels are much better outside than in India, I would say, definitely. And plus, when you get a lot of when the currency depreciates, it gives us also an advantage to be competitive. So definitely, I would say margins a

items.statement: Solar business profitability is 3-4 points below other businesses.
items.quote: But I would say that it would be let's say, three to four points below our other business. This is what it is.

items.statement: Invested ₹7 crore in a Mazak machine for mechanical seals, running three shifts.
items.quote: We have invested in a machine, Mazak machine specifically for that, which is running three shifts almost an investment of ₹7 Cr on that machine alone.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission extension from ₹3 lakh crore to ₹8 lakh crore provides good opportunity.
items.quote: So, the government approved the Jal Jeevan Mission extension from 3 lakh to almost 8 lakh crore now.

items.statement: Thermal power pumps account for 3-4% of total plant size, up to 3-5% in any project.
items.quote: I would say, normally, pumps in a thermal power plant is 3% to 4% of the total size of the power plant and same would be in any maximum up to 3% to 5% in any project would be the quantum or value wise of the pumps, which are there.

items.statement: NPCIL is looking for alternative suppliers for reactor coolant pumps, which will be future competition.
items.quote: Yes, definitely, NPCIL is looking for alternative suppliers. So, I think there are development orders given and there are companies which have approached and which have discussed with NPCIL. So, yes, those vendors, if and when they are approved, will be a competition to us also.

items.statement: Reciprocating pump business expected to flourish in FY27-FY28 after getting approvals.
items.quote: And we are halfway through it. And this business in '27 '28 should flourish much better.

items.statement: Mechanical seals business currently ₹15 crore, growing healthily with 9,000-10,000 seals manufactured.
items.quote: Today, we have, if I have to give a figure, around ₹15 crores of it is business. It is a starting and because we are not into API seals, we are m ore into non-API seals. So that business is growing healthily.

items.statement: Mining pumps order book is ₹15-20 crore, expected to grow year-on-year.
items.quote: The order book position is maybe ₹15 crores, ₹20 crores is something which is there. It's not big when you compare to the other thing, other segments. But I feel it will grow year-on-year as we increase our installed base and also we grow in our exports.

items.statement: Expect cement demand growth of 7-8% in Gujarat; company aims to grow 150-200% of market growth rate
items.quote: Industry growth, keeping in view the market demand and the infrastructure projects which are under pipeline, so, market will grow by 7 % to 8%. So, definitely we will grow at least 150% or 200% from the market.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton dip of ~INR200 on purchased clinker vs own clinker; blended portfolio (55% clinker factor) mitigates impact
items.quote: There would be a slightly dip of about INR200 per metric ton, Raj.

items.statement: No immediate clinker plant expansion; will evaluate when capacity utilization reaches 70-75%
items.quote: when we will reach close to the 70 %, 75% of the capacity utilization, we will explore the option of the future capex.

items.statement: Gujarat monthly demand ~2.7 mt; Saurashtra infrastructure projects (Jamnagar, Rajkot) driving 8-10% demand growth
items.quote: every month there is a demand of 27 lakhs ton of the cement. And with the upcoming infrastructure projects, we are expecting demand would increase to about 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Plan to increase digital HCP reach by 50,000 doctors
items.quote: Digital reach in addition to 50,000 HCPs, from where we are today, to really scale up our HCP engagement efforts in the category.

items.statement: Revenue grew 21%, Operating Profit up 13%, PAT up 33% in 2025
items.quote: Our Revenue from Operations has gone up by 21%, Operating Profit up by 13% and a 33% increase on PAT.

items.statement: Domestic sales grew 22% in quarter; excluding recalls, growth was 11%
items.quote: If you see the quarter for domestic sales, it grew by 22%, and you remove the recall from there. Without recall, the growth is 11%.

items.statement: Launched Allegra D last year; evaluating pipeline for meaningful innovations in core categories
items.quote: One case in point was the launch of Allegra D, which just happened last year, which was one of the unique formulations that you see in the India market.

items.statement: OTC policy still in works; will unlock direct consumer communication when approved
items.quote: As you're aware, the OTC policy is still in the works. And of course, we are expecting that it will come out very soon.

items.statement: Almost 100% production happens in India; fully independent supply chain operations
items.quote: Most of our production, almost 100% happens in India. So, we are not really dependent in any way on any global supplies that happen.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic opportunities but need to answer make vs buy questions first
items.quote: We do keep looking at these options. Global is absolutely open to these discussions. But we need to answer a few questions before we go ahead with that.

items.statement: E-commerce and modern trade still single-digit contribution but growing faster than core business
items.quote: We have started work on e-commerce and modern trade, but it's still in single digit in terms of contribution to the business. But we are listed across platforms today, where you will find most of our brands, but growing much faster than the core business.

items.statement: Combiflam cream allows direct consumer communication; used for Lalbaugcha Raja event
items.quote: The Combiflam cream is a portfolio that we have. It is a part of the Combiflam portfolio where you are allowed to talk to consumers directly.

items.statement: Field force of ~350 medical reps; evaluating productivity gains and third-party models for reach expansion
items.quote: So, 350 odd people today, medical reps that we have going outside.

items.statement: Recalled products back in market; 2 of 4 brands recovered to pre-recall run rates, others growing fast
items.quote: Out of the 4, almost 2 have already reached it. On a couple of them, honestly, and that's the feedback coming from HCPs, they were delighted that we had come back.

items.statement: Growth and penetration is clear agenda for India; profitable growth achieved in 2025
items.quote: Growth is the agenda for India, very clearly. But having said that, it's also profitable growth. And that's what we've also achieved over the last one year.
